Series::linearalg¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series::linearalg -> Series::LinearAlgAccessor

Series::linearalg() -> SeriesLinearAlgProxy
Series::linearalg(const Series& other) -> SeriesLinearAlgProxy

What It Does¶

linearalg is a namespace-like accessor for vector and matrix operations. It does not compute a value by itself. It selects the linear-algebra method family and keeps the owning Series as the left operand.

The distinction matters because these methods do not use one common elementwise shape rule. A matrix product contracts dimensions, a batched matrix product broadcasts only its batch dimensions, and a dot product requires two equally long vectors and reduces them to a scalar. The accessor gives those related rules one visible home.

How The Accessor Organizes Matrix Work¶

Think of linearalg as a door, not an operation. The owning Series stays on the left side of every binary operation; the accessor chooses a family in which dimensions have algebraic roles:

  • a vector dimension is contracted by an inner product

  • a matrix’s last two dimensions mean rows and columns

  • leading dimensions in matmul() identify batches of independent products

  • strict methods such as mm(), mv(), and dot() reject ranks that would change the intended operation

That distinction is why linearalg deserves its own reference. Elementwise mul() asks which positions broadcast together. Linear-algebra products ask which dimensions contract and which survive in the output.

Calling Styles¶

The dot-style form passes peers to individual methods:

auto result = left.linearalg.matmul(right);

The proxy style binds a peer first:

auto result = left.linearalg(right).matmul();

Both calls treat left as the left operand and right as the right operand. Binding a peer does not reverse the order.

Unary methods do not need a peer:

auto determinant = matrix.linearalg.det();
auto same_result = matrix.linearalg().det();

The complete accessor surface is documented: products, norms, determinants, matrix transformations, factorizations, and structured or general solves.

Use the Series::LinearAlgAccessor API Reference as the landing page for this family. Each accessor method is documented there on its own page:

  • rank-polymorphic multiplication: matmul()

  • strict matrix products: mm() and mv()

  • vector inner products: dot() and vdot()

  • determinant values: det(), logdet(), and slogdet()

  • matrix inversion: inverse()

  • integer and continuous matrix transforms: matrix_power() and matrix_exp()

  • rectangular and rank-deficient reversal: pinverse()

  • global magnitude: norm()

  • positive-definite factorization: cholesky()

  • orthogonal-triangular factorization: qr_q() and qr_r()

  • singular-value decomposition: svd(), svd_u(), svd_s(), and svd_vh()

  • structured and general systems: triangular_solve(), cholesky_solve(), cholesky_inverse(), and lu_solve()

Returns¶

Series::LinearAlgAccessor or SeriesLinearAlgProxy A lightweight method-selection object bound to the owning Series, and optionally to a peer Series.

Accessing `linearalg` does not copy numeric data and does not mutate the
owner.

Example¶

The two binary call styles are equivalent.

auto left = pluss::make_series({{1.0, 2.0}, {3.0, 4.0}});
auto right = pluss::make_series({{2.0, 0.0}, {1.0, 2.0}});

std::cout << "peer_argument=" << left.linearalg.mm(right) << "\n";
std::cout << "peer_bound=" << left.linearalg(right).mm() << "\n";

Output¶

peer_argument=pluss::Series(shape=[2,2], strides=[2,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[[4, 4],
  [10, 8]]
peer_bound=pluss::Series(shape=[2,2], strides=[2,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[[4, 4],
  [10, 8]]

The accessor is bound to left, so both forms calculate left * right. This is observable with non-commuting matrices: changing which object owns the accessor can change the result.

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • linearalg is an accessor, not a materialized result.

  • A peer-bound zero-argument binary method requires a peer to have been passed to linearalg(...) first.

  • The owner remains the left operand. This is important for non-commutative methods such as matrix multiplication and linear solves.

  • Individual methods still enforce their own shape, dtype, platform, and decomposition requirements.
